narrative.death:
The dust of the ridge is the last thing you see.
Start a new game to try again.

start_questions.name: Background
start_questions.text: Before the caravan, who were you?

options.text: A caravan guard, hired at the southern wells.
A merchant's child, sent north with a little silver.
A temple scribe, who reads the old letters.

evidence.name: Wheel ruts
evidence.description: Deep ruts lead from the cold camp to a fork in the track that no map shows.

evidence.name: Displaced cargo
evidence.description: The bandits' crates carry the lost wagons' seal; they found them scattered beyond the fork, not taken from wagons.

evidence.name: Rask's account
evidence.description: Rask swears the crates lay in the grass past the fork, with no wagons and no tracks leading away.

evidence.name: The impossible fork
evidence.description: A second road branches east where the land should allow none, paved with stones older than Thornwick.

evidence.name: Ennick's account
evidence.description: The drover Ennick saw the lead wagons take the east branch at dusk. By morning the branch was gone.

evidence.name: Strange stonework
evidence.description: A low ring of fitted stones on the hill where the east road ends. The caravan's tracks stop at its threshold.

evidence.name: The Dawn Hall's reading
evidence.description: Sister Ama calls the ring a drowned-god shrine: a road that opens to prayer and closes behind the faithless.

evidence.name: The archivist's reading
evidence.description: Archivist Tenko names the stones a milestone of an older road, built and then hidden, running north.

evidence.name: The hill-folk reading
evidence.description: Old Garrow says the hill folk leave the rings alone, because the roads between them walk at night.

outcomes.name: The first chapter closes
outcomes.text: You have chosen your road. The rest of the realm waits beyond Thornwick's walls. (End of the slice.)
